items.question: How long must meditation be applied after worshipping this circle?
premises: The practice continues for a duration
items.inference: Meditation on the circle is to be sustained continuously after its worship.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible during this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practitioner perceives diverse languages, both familiar and unfamiliar.
uncertainties: Agreement between bhāṣās (feminine) and aśrutāni/śrutāni (neuter) is unusual but taken as describing the languages.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard before, arise.

items.question: By whom and within whom are these languages spontaneously heard?
premises: The self is the agent and recipient
The hearing takes place within the self
items.inference: The languages are heard spontaneously by the self, to the self, and within the self.
items.plain_english: They are heard spontaneously by oneself, to oneself, and within oneself.

items.question: What physical transformation results from the preceding meditative attainment?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair
The practitioner is compared to Kāma
The practitioner is like a second Kāma
items.inference: The practitioner attains a youthful, beautiful form like a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes like a second god of love.

items.question: What effect on speech results from destroying the wind and related forces?
premises: The wind and related forces are to be destroyed
The person stands like a mute
items.inference: By destroying the wind and related forces through speech, one renders the target mute.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vāyvādeḥ and the mechanism of nāśayet vācā are context-dependent.
items.plain_english: One should destroy the wind and so forth by speech; indeed, he then stands like a mute.

items.question: What supreme power is attributed to the seventh circle addressed to the goddess?
premises: The seventh circle is being described
It is addressed to the goddess
It causes the paralysis of armies
items.inference: The seventh circle is supreme and has the power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: One devoted to worship and meditation in that circle gains vision from afar.
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation in that circle, vision arises from afar.

items.question: Which magical powers become available through the practices described to the beloved?
items.inference: The practice grants powers such as killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and the like.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and such powers become possible.

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in the eight-times-eight method?
premises: The eight-times-eight method must be known
items.inference: Success in this method depends exclusively on knowing the eight-times-eight procedure.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight times eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the teaching declared without doubt be firmly ascertained?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt
Devotion and reasoning are the means
items.inference: The doubtless teaching must be ascertained through both devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this has been declared by me without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the eighth chapter in the Candradvīpa text.
items.plain_english: In the text emerged from Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

items.question: What teaching about the yoginīs will be explained to the beloved next?
premises: The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: Which collective domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: They belong to a complete field-group
items.inference: The complete field-group comprises all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.
uncertainties: The exact technical meaning of sarvakṣetrakam depends on tantric context.
items.plain_english: The complete field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are enumerated as part of this arrangement?
items.inference: The arrangement includes all innate, all family-born, and all door-guardian yoginīs.
uncertainties: sarvakulajā appears in singular-like form but is taken as plural in this list.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all the family-born ones, and all the door-guardians.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among all secrets been revealed?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets
The revelation is due to devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret of secrets has been revealed because of the recipient's devotion.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret of secrets has been revealed because of your devotion.

items.question: What instruction does the speaker now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish now
The wish is to hear from the gurus
The topic is the worship of the siddhas
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of two syllables be transmitted?
premises: There is an arrangement of two syllables
items.inference: The arrangement of two syllables should be transmitted to others in the appropriate context.
uncertainties: The precise meaning of anyanteṣu is ambiguous without wider context.
items.plain_english: One should give the arrangement of the two syllables among others.

items.question: What claim is made about the uniqueness of this knowledge in the future?
premises: This knowledge is taken as the standard
No equal knowledge exists now by implication
No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: No knowledge equal to this will ever exist again.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain to the beautiful-eyed one?
premises: The topic is the method of their names
The addressee is asked to listen
items.inference: The speaker promises to explain the method of their names to the listener.
uncertainties: The referent of teṣāṃ depends on preceding context.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen; I shall speak the method of their names.

items.question: Who are identified as the independent impellers of the lineage across the four ages?
premises: They are addressed to the lord
They are independent impellers of the lineage
items.inference: The independent impellers of the lineage are identified in relation to the four ages.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of caturyuga iti is compressed and context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Thus, O Lord, they are the independent impellers of the lineage through the four ages.

items.question: What is the extent and origin of this Kaula teaching?
premises: It has arisen from the supreme
items.inference: This Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, extends to ten crores in measure.
uncertainties: The unit implied by daśakoṭipramāṇaṃ (verses, mantras, etc.) is not specified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, measures ten crores.

items.question: By whose agency and will did the yoginī named Icchā extend up to māyā?
premises: The action reaches up to māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, extended up to māyā.
uncertainties: The verbal action governing māyāntaṃ is implicit.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the siddhas and by supreme will, reached up to māyā.

items.question: By whom was the teaching concerning the mothers transmitted again?
items.inference: The teaching concerning the mothers was told again by the sky-movers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again to the mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs described as good eaters?
premises: They are described as good eaters
items.inference: The teaching was told to the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
uncertainties: The instrumental form bhūcarī is unusual; taken as agent by context.
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told to the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
